newLayers.name: Hadoop IO and Commit Protocols
newLayers.description: How Spark reads and writes files through Hadoop APIs: compression codecs and IO stream helpers, input formats and record readers for whole text files, fixed length binary files and portable data streams, and the commit protocols (FileCommitProtocol and its Hadoop implementations, SparkHadoopWriter) that make job output atomic.

appendDesc.RDD Library and Shared Variables: Also covers approximate results (PartialResult and the evaluators for count, mean and sum), asynchronous RDD actions, BlockRDD and BinaryFileRDD.

tour.title: Writing files: commit protocols
tour.description: saveAsHadoopFile and the DataFrame file writers do not write to the final directory directly. A FileCommitProtocol creates temporary files for each task attempt, commits a task by moving its files, and commits the job at the end (or aborts it), so output appears atomically. HadoopMapReduceCommitProtocol and HadoopMapRedCommitProtocol implement it on top of the Hadoop output committers, and SparkHadoopWriter runs the write tasks for an RDD and applies the protocol.
